answer: I'd like to talk about a piece of furniture that most visitors wouldn't even notice. A piece of furniture I am genuinely fond of is a large, comfortable armchair in the corner of my room. It is old and a little worn, but it is easily my favourite spot in the entire flat. It used to sit in our living room when I was a child, and when my parents bought a new sofa set, I rescued it before it could be given away. I positioned it right beside a window, so I get plenty of natural light and a pleasant view of the quiet street below our third-floor flat. I use it mainly for reading, and it has become my personal little [[retreat]]. After a long day at the consultancy, I often sit there with a book, or simply listen to music with my eyes closed. My younger sister occasionally borrows it to revise for her exams, though she always gives it back rather [[reluctantly]]. What I love about it is how wonderfully comfortable it is; I can [[sink into]] it for hours without any discomfort. There is something deeply [[cosy]] about having a dedicated chair just for relaxing and reading. Honestly, some of my most peaceful moments have been spent in that chair with a good book and a cup of tea. It might not be the most stylish piece of furniture, but its comfort makes it [[invaluable]] to me. I think everyone needs a favourite spot like this, and that chair is undoubtedly mine.

followUps.q: Would you ever replace the chair?
followUps.answer: Not unless it completely falls apart. It has been [[reupholstered]] once already, and I'd happily do that again rather than buy a new one, because a new chair simply wouldn't feel the same.

followUps.q: Do you prefer modern or traditional furniture?
followUps.answer: I prefer traditional wooden furniture, the kind that lasts for generations. My grandparents still have a carved wooden bed in the village that's older than my father, and it's still perfectly solid.
